## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sakuṇajātaka* (Ja 36), translated in English as *The Bird*, is a birth-story belonging to the Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework recorded in the tradition, the story was delivered by the Buddha while staying at Jetavana, occasioned by a monk whose monastic cell had burned down [SuttaCentral]. The narrative opens in translation with the verse line "Ye denizens of air" [SuttaCentral].
None of the references in the examined secondary literature discuss this specific text, instead referring to other bird-related stories such as the *Tesakuṇajātaka* (Ja 521) or *Javasakuṇajātaka* (Ja 308).
